questions.question:
D1 — Add gstack skill routing rules to this project's CLAUDE.md?
Project/branch/task: fixture repo on main; one-time gstack onboarding, unrelated to the plan itself.
ELI10: gstack works best when CLAUDE.md tells Claude which skill to reach for ("bugs → /investigate", "scope → /plan-ceo-review"). Without it you invoke skills by hand. This is a small appended section plus a commit.
Stakes if we pick wrong: none for this review; only affects how automatically skills get suggested later. Note: plan mode blocks file edits and commits right now, so if you pick A the append + commit happens after this review exits plan mode.
Recommendation: A because it is a two-way door and costs one small commit.
Note: options differ in kind, not coverage — no completeness score.
Net: convenience later vs. one extra commit in a fixture repo.

options.label: Add routing rules (recommended)
options.description: ✅ Skills get suggested automatically when a request matches (bugs, scope, ship, review). ✅ One appended section, one commit, fully reversible by deleting it. ❌ Adds ~20 lines to CLAUDE.md in what is currently a small fixture repo.

options.label: No thanks, manual invocation
options.description: ✅ CLAUDE.md stays exactly as seeded; nothing else changes in the repo. ✅ You can re-enable later with gstack-config set routing_declined false. ❌ Skills only run when you type them; no proactive routing suggestions.

questions.question:
D2 — Which review mode for the saved-views plan?
Project/branch/task: main; reviewing PLAN.md "Add saved project views" (per-member named filter+sort presets on a project task list).
ELI10: The mode sets my posture. It does not approve any scope or approach change; every addition or cut still gets its own yes/no. This is an enhancement to an existing task list, estimated ~10–14 changed files (estimate; no code in this checkout), which under the skill's rules points to SELECTIVE EXPANSION: make the current scope bulletproof, then offer a short list of adjacent additions (shared views, URL-addressable filter state, default view, handling deleted filter targets) one at a time for you to take, defer, or skip.
Stakes if we pick wrong: too ambitious and a small feature turns into a views platform; too narrow and you ship a table whose schema can't grow into shared views without a migration.
Recommendation: SELECTIVE EXPANSION because the core is clear and small, and the real leverage is in a few cheap adjacent decisions (schema shape, URL state) that are painful to retrofit.
Note: options differ in kind, not coverage — no completeness score.
Net: rigor on the core plus a neutral menu of expansions, versus dreaming big, holding the line, or cutting.

options.label: SELECTIVE EXPANSION (recommended)
options.description: ✅ Full rigor on the submitted scope (errors, edge cases, tests, observability) plus a neutral cherry-pick menu of adjacent additions. ✅ Accepted items become scope; rejected ones are recorded as NOT in scope so nothing creeps back. ❌ More questions than HOLD SCOPE; each expansion is its own decision.

options.label: SCOPE EXPANSION
options.description: ✅ Dream-big pass: 10x vision, platonic ideal, delight scan, then opt-in per proposal. ✅ Best if you suspect saved views should become a views platform (shared, default, subscriptions). ❌ Risks turning a two-week pilot feature into a multi-sprint initiative.

options.label: HOLD SCOPE
options.description: ✅ Maximum rigor on exactly the four bullets in the plan; no expansion menu. ✅ Fastest path to an approved plan. ❌ Schema-shaping choices (owner/visibility column, URL state) only surface if I flag them as failure modes, not as offers.

options.label: SCOPE REDUCTION
options.description: ✅ Strip to the minimum that removes the pain (possibly bookmarkable filter URLs with no table). ✅ Smallest diff, least to maintain. ❌ Probably loses the in-app picker the goal asks for; only fits if the file count or timeline is under real pressure.
